record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Fix an integer k ≥ 4. Beyond the currently known polygonal examples, are there other k-reflective projective billiards inside domains belonging to specified boundary-regularity classes such as polygonal, piecewise-algebraic, or analytic domains?

evidence.quote: Question 2 (Projective Ivrii’s conjecture): Given an integer k ≥ 4, are there other examples of k-reflective projective billiards within a class of domains with a specific boundary smoothness (polygonal, piecewise-algebraic or analytic, etc.)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A planar projective billiard is a domain Ω ⊂ ℝℙ² (or ℝ²) bounded by a piecewise-smooth curve ∂Ω together with a smooth field of transverse lines along ∂Ω (the "projective field"). The reflection law of the projective billiard is defined as follows: an incoming oriented line ℓ hitting ∂Ω at a smooth point p reflects to the unique outgoing line ℓ' such that the four lines (ℓ, ℓ', the tangent line T_p∂Ω, and the projective line at p) form a harmonic quadruple in the pencil of lines through p. (When the projective field is the field of normals, this reduces to the usual law of optical reflection.)

A k-periodic orbit (k ≥ 2) is a closed polygonal trajectory P₁P₂…P_kP₁ with vertices on ∂Ω whose successive sides obey the projective reflection law at each P_i. The projective billiard is called k-reflective if the set of k-periodic orbits has nonempty interior in the phase space of oriented lines meeting ∂Ω (equivalently, there is an open 2-parameter family of k-periodic orbits).

Currently, the only known k-reflective planar projective billiards (for k ≥ 4) are certain polygonal constructions.

Question. Fix an integer k ≥ 4. Do there exist k-reflective planar projective billiards on domains Ω whose boundary belongs to one of the following regularity classes, beyond the known polygonal examples:
(a) polygonal domains (i.e., are there essentially new polygonal k-reflective projective billiards);
(b) piecewise-algebraic domains (boundary consisting of finitely many real-algebraic arcs);
(c) (real-)analytic domains (boundary a real-analytic curve)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Fierobe and collaborators, 2020–2024) constructed polygonal counterexamples to the projective Ivrii conjecture for k=3 and even k≥4, and proved non-existence in some higher-dimensional / smooth settings. However, the general question of finding new k-reflective projective billiards (k≥4) within the polygonal, piecewise-algebraic, or analytic boundary classes — beyond the known polygonal constructions — remains stated as an open problem in the recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Examples of projective billiards with open sets of periodic orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Counter-examples are polygons admitting a 2-parameter family of n-periodic orbits with n=3 or any even integer ≥4.
status_evidence.claim: Known k-reflective projective billiards (k≥4) are polygonal.

status_evidence.title: Examples of reflective projective billiards and outer ghost billiards
status_evidence.claim: Polygonal examples exist; other regularity classes remain unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Billiards and Geometric Optics
status_evidence.snippet: Question 2 (Projective Ivrii's conjecture): Given an integer k≥4, are there other examples of k-reflective projective billiards within a class of domains with specific boundary smoothness?
